headline: Residue-level metrics gauge AlphaFold reliability and context-dependent local structure
label: Structural Protein Model Analysis
summary: Whole-proteome AlphaFold predictions demand quantitative per-residue reliability checks that account for structural context.
synthesis: The three preprints apply quantitative, residue-level analysis to protein structure rather than descriptive cataloguing. Two evaluate AlphaFold predictions: one introduces arity maps from Wasserstein PCA of per-residue neighbor histograms to separate AlphaFold-DB models into folded, disordered, and implausible groups, while the other proposes topological and combinatorial measures to identify coherent sequence stretches in pLDDT confidence profiles. The third compares residue interaction networks of remote homologous domains across different multi-domain architectures and reports that neighboring domains alter local network features. The dominant thread is reliability assessment of predicted structures and the dependence of local organization on structural context. The published orphan-gene classifier paper falls outside this structural thread. What is new here is the emphasis on context-dependence and reliability, rather than structure cataloguing alone.
